Isotropic specialization and fourth-moment identity prove the finite distribution and two-point phenomenon; rational exhaustive checks agree.

originality.rationale: Original Algorithm 1 supplies sign sketch and residual probes, and the 2021 follow-up supplies primary MSC 65C05 and explicit discussion of flat spectra. The 2016 deflation paper establishes that deflation can raise variance under random-unitary spectral models; that phenomenon and diagonal Hutchinson exactness are excluded from claimed novelty. Neither source gives the all-spectrum deterministic conditional law of the data-dependent one-column Rademacher sketch or its bivariate sign-sum distribution; the qualitative modern note similarly does not imply the formula. Indexed searches found no equivalent or dominating result.
residual_risks: The all-diagonal rank-one identity is elementary enough that unindexed lecture notes may independently derive it.
The result is not a high-query Hutch++ performance bound and does not transfer to general non-diagonal matrices.
The original algorithm and primary follow-up may have software variants not covered by this exactly specified sign-sketch version.

value.rationale: The one-column sketch is the published algorithm’s smallest full three-matvec run, and the diagonal class is exactly where plain sign-probe trace estimation is noise-free. An exact entire output law for every positive diagonal spectrum, not just a variance example, isolates the effect of sketch-based control variates in this natural low-budget regime. The weighted-Rademacher formula computes finite-sample risk and shows a sharp nonzero deterministic absolute error on a 2x2 isotropic input, and a nondegenerate chi-square absolute-error limit at fixed probe count as dimension grows. This supports quantitative low-budget trace-estimation method selection.
